**2026-11-19.** **A synchronous HTTP answer sets its own status and headers** with
`<q:reply status="…">` and the reply's `<q:header>` children. This adds an attribute to the frozen
`q:` namespace (`urn:sutra:q:1.0`), which is why the release is 0.8.0. The addition is backward
compatible: existing packages load and run unchanged, and an answer without the attribute or
headers is unchanged. **Broker outages can reach the deployment as messages**
(`sutra.engine.connectivity-events.channel`). **FEEL durations keep fractional seconds.** No
migration, and no archive or snapshot format change.

**There is no 0.7.0 engine image.** The v0.7.0 tag, its CLI archives and its crates.io crates were
published, but the release run stopped at the engine image scan on a base-image advisory published
the same day (CVE-2026-95690, see Image scan below), so no
`ghcr.io/startr-trade/sutra:0.7.0` image and no 0.7.0 GitHub Release exist. 0.8.0 carries every
0.7.0 change: an image user on 0.6.25 moves straight to 0.8.0 and reads the 0.7.0 notes too.

## Before you upgrade

**Check these against what you run:**

- **Coming from the 0.6.25 image:** everything in the 0.7.0 notes applies (revisions seeded from the
  database clock, migration V103, uncorrelated messages logged and audited).
- **A FEEL duration with a fraction on a unit other than seconds is now refused.**
  `duration("PT1.5H")` used to be cut to `PT1H`; it is now an error (`duration() cannot parse the
  string`), as XML Schema and the FEEL specification require. Write `PT1H30M`, or `PT5400S`.
- **`.seconds` on a days-and-time duration returns the fraction.** `duration("PT4.5S").seconds` is
  `4.5`, where it was `4`. An expression that relied on it being whole should apply `floor()`.
- **A fractional seconds value is no longer dropped.** `duration("PT0.001S")` was zero, so a FEEL
  timer expression that returned it fired at once; it now waits 1 ms. `string()` of such a duration
  keeps the fraction (`PT0.001S`).

## Status and headers on a synchronous answer (`q:` addition)

On an HTTP channel that answers synchronously (`ack-mode: on-complete`, the default), a `<q:reply>`
with no `destination` can set the status, and its `<q:header>` children become the response's
headers:

```xml
<q:reply contentType="application/json" status="201">
  <q:header name="Location" value="'/items/' + req.id"/>
</q:reply>
```

`status` is literal first, else FEEL: digits alone are the status, anything else is an expression
(`"if found then 200 else 404"`) that must give a whole number or a string of digits; `null` keeps
200. A reply that declares a status or headers answers with them even when the flow rendered no
body, so an auth check can answer 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` and no template.

| Rule | At load (`sutra lint`, sealing, deploy) | At the answer |
|---|---|---|
| The status is 200–599 | a literal outside is refused | a value outside, a fraction or a non-number is a 500 |
| A 3xx needs a `Location` | a literal 3xx with no `Location` header is refused | a 3xx whose `Location` is `null` is a 500 |
| A 204 or 304 has no body | — | body and `Content-Type` are not sent |
| A header name is an HTTP token, and not `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Connection`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Upgrade`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Type` or `Sutra-*` | refused | — |
| A header value has no control character | — | a 500 |

The codes are `SUTRA.OUTBOUND.REPLY_STATUS_INVALID` and `SUTRA.OUTBOUND.REPLY_HEADER_INVALID`; the
500 names the header, never its value. The status applies at the end of a flow, at
`<q:reply continue="true">`, and on a relayed turn's answer. An `ack-mode: on-persist` channel still
answers 202 and adds the headers; a broker intake has no status; `sutra lint` warns about both
(`SUTRA.CHANNEL.REPLY_STATUS_IGNORED`).

Library surface: `sutra_channels::reply_head` (the rules, shared by the lint and the HTTP answer);
`SyncReply` gains `status`, `headers` and `has_body`; `ReplyBinding` gains `status`.

## Broker connectivity events

With `sutra.engine.connectivity-events.channel` (env `SUTRA_CONNECTIVITY_EVENTS_CHANNEL`) set, each
broker outage start and end a transport sees on one of a deployment's channels is delivered to that
deployment as a JSON message on the channel of that name, if the deployment declares one (declare it
`transport: local`, `codec: json`). The message carries `code` (the transport's log code), `channel`,
`direction` (`inbound` or `outbound`), `state` (`down` or `up`), `startedAt`, and on `up` also
`endedAt` and `ms`, plus `detail`. A deployment receives events only for its own channels.

The AMQP 1.0 transport reports its intakes, and each send channel that sent during an outage (its
window ends on its first send that reaches the broker again). Delivery is best effort: 1024 events
queue per deployment, the oldest dropped past that (`SUTRA.CONNECTIVITY.EVENTS_DROPPED`); an event
the deployment refuses is logged as `SUTRA.CONNECTIVITY.EVENT_UNDELIVERED` and not retried. Unset,
nothing is collected.

Transport SPI: `ConnectivityReporter`, `ConnectivityEvent` and `current_send()` in
`sutra_channels::connectivity` (re-exported by `sutra-transport-spi`), plus the default method
`InboundIntake::connectivity()`, a no-op unless the engine installs a sink. Existing transports
compile unchanged and report nothing.

## Fixed

- **FEEL durations keep fractional seconds.** The parser dropped everything after the decimal point,
  so `duration("PT0.001S")` was zero. A days-and-time duration now holds its seconds to the
  nanosecond (digits past the ninth are truncated) through parsing, `string()`
  (`P1DT2H3M4.123456789S`), comparison, arithmetic with dates, times and durations, multiplication
  and division by a number, and the `seconds` accessor. Seconds accept XML Schema's decimal forms
  (`PT0.5S`, `PT.5S`, `PT0.S`). The DMN TCK results are unchanged.

## Image scan

CVE-2026-95690 (libssl3, DTLS) in the distroless base has no fixed Debian package. The engine never
loads libssl3: re-checked on the 0.8.0 binary, `readelf -d` lists libgcc_s, libm, libc and the
loader as its only libraries and the binary holds no libssl name to load at run time, and nothing in
it speaks DTLS (the Kafka client's compiled-in OpenSSL is TLS over TCP). It is time-boxed in
`.trivyignore.yaml` with the other base-image entries, to 2026-12-16.

## Known

- **`SUTRA.INBOUND.CAPABILITY_MISMATCH` answers HTTP 500.** Unchanged from 0.6.23; a later release
  will answer it with 415.
